title: Forest Fire Lookout Association, New York State Chapter
license: No licence stated; facts only (dates, names, the kind of work done). Every note is our own wording and every event links to the chapter newsletter it comes from. Positions are copied from the NHLR and FFLA records (the chapter publishes none).

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association, New York State Chapter

credit: Forest Fire Lookout Association, New York State Chapter (nysffla.org)

events.note: A 22-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower was erected on Ampersand Mountain, the only NY tower built in 1921.
The Ampersand tower was closed to service in 1970.
The Ampersand tower was removed in 1977.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association, New York State Chapter

events.note: The tower was first built in 1918; the Friends celebrated its centennial in 2018.
Existing observer's cabin repaired and put in first-class shape in 1922 as part of the new observer housing standard.
A Student Conservation Association crew recently painted the tower, according to photos on the Friends of Azure Mountain website (reported Aug 2017).
The security fencing on the tower was replaced by Dave Vana and a helper (13 hours of work) as a centennial present, before the July 2018 celebration.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association, New York State Chapter

events.note: The Balsam Lake Club built a log observatory on the summit in 1887, widely considered New York's first fire tower.
The first log observatory was found in ruins in 1901, believed to have been struck by lightning and burned.
A second log observatory was built on the summit in the summer of 1905 by club wardens and neighbors.
When the state took over, a small observer's cabin, telephone line and summit road were added in 1909.
The first steel tower was erected on the summit in 1919, with materials hauled up by wagon.
In mid-October 1999 NYSDEC staff and Americorps carried in eight new galvanized cross braces, bolts for the whole tower and windows for its restoration.
Balsam Lake tower reopened June 3, 2000 after restoration under the Catskill Fire Tower Project.
In early May 2016 volunteers stained the observer's cabin and made other repairs while hauling donated lumber to the summit for later landing and step replacement.
Some painting and cleaning was reported done at Balsam Lake Mountain around the May 15, 2021 steward orientation.
NYS Forest Rangers and volunteers replaced badly deteriorated landing boards on Balsam Lake tower in fall 2022.
NYSDEC closed the observer's cabin museum for repairs, and a cab window that blew out over the winter was given a temporary fix at the spring inspection.
DEC Operations staff installed new operable windows in the Balsam Lake tower cab, replacing badly worn ones (reported autumn 2023).
An engineer inspected the observer's cabin and the final report reached DEC on Sept. 9; it found the restoration work 'extensive'.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association, New York State Chapter

events.note: NYSDEC closed Beebe Hill tower after a windstorm blew part of the roof off, pending repairs.
NYSDEC Region 4 refurbished the tower (roof repairs briefly closed it) and replaced the observer's cabin windows, roof and siding; shown at an October picnic (work year reported).

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association, New York State Chapter

events.note: FFLA volunteers made two trips, with DEC permission, to cover graffiti in the Belfry tower cab (reported).

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association, New York State Chapter

events.note: CCC crews began building the 60-foot International Derrick tower; the observer's cabin, road and phone line followed that year.
The Berry Hill tower was closed to the public from Oct 19, 2020 while restoration work began on site.
Antennas were taken off the tower and it was restored for reopening under a DEC-funded project (mostly done by 2 July); graffiti in the cab was cleaned up by September.
FFLA volunteers stained the observer's cabin in two work days using NYSDEC-supplied stain (reported June 2026).

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association, New York State Chapter

The tower was closed in 1988 and remains closed to the public.
A 39-foot antenna was installed above the cab in 1988 to help State Police communications.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association, New York State Chapter

events.note: By 1994 the Blue Mt Fire Tower Restoration Committee and DEC had restored and reopened the tower (new windows, scraping, painting, new wood); the roof blew off soon after and was replaced.
NYSDEC removed the equipment attached to and under the tower in fall 2017 to return it to its historic appearance (reported).
FFLA, NYSDEC and Team Rubicon volunteers worked on the tower on 1-2 June and FFLA volunteers painted it on 8 July, completing the year's major restoration.
After graffiti was reported on the tower, cab, cabin foundation and summit rocks, FFLA volunteers went up and cleaned what they could in poor weather (reported).
On May 15, 2021 a crew removed the old siding on the Blue Mountain observer's cabin and installed new; exterior work, incl. replacing floor joists, finished that week.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association, New York State Chapter

The 80-foot Aermotor tower was re-erected on its original summit by Excelsior Towers, becoming visible above the trees Oct. 17; opened to hikers by early 2025.

Buck Mountain tower opened to the public on Sept 2, 2023 after the Town of Long Lake's restoration and trail project; ribbon cutting Sept 15.

Chapter volunteers painted over significant graffiti in Dickinson Hill tower before the Labor Day holiday weekend.
On April 21, 2023 chapter volunteers painted over graffiti in the Dickinson Hill tower cab.
Park staff and FFLA stewards repainted the tower and replaced its steps and landings over the summer under a Friends of Grafton Lakes grant.

NYSDEC Region 4 rehabilitated the tower before its centennial: new roof and fresh paint, plus new windows per a later issue, funded by a $48,000 Adventure NY grant.
NYSDEC Region 4 Operations staff built a new front porch on the observer's cabin in summer 2018.
DEC Region 4 installed new windows and siding on the observer's cabin as part of a large cabin preservation effort.

Friends of Hurricane volunteers painted the whole tower with silver protective paint, paid for by NYSDEC.
A new roof, made by the Friends and flown up with state funding, was installed on July 31 by David Vana's crew just before the centennial.
Friends of Hurricane Mountain hung panoramic photos in the tower cab in September 2020 after an August attempt failed over mounting hardware.
A new map table was carried up and installed in the Hurricane tower cab on Sept 4, 2021, similar to the observer's original.
Friends of Hurricane replaced the 2015 safety wire with heavier wire on all four landings after winter ice damage (reported in June 2024).

A donated replica map and an FFLA-funded map table were installed in the cab for the centennial; the map was pulled for moisture damage in autumn, repaired and returned.
FFLA volunteers gave the observer's cabin a fresh coat of stain ahead of the August centennial.

The wooden tower was replaced in 1916 by a 40-foot steel Aermotor LL25, one of the first ten steel towers in NYS.
The tower was closed in 1970 after serving fire spotting; it was later dismantled and sold on.

association.name: Forest Fire Lookout Association, New York State Chapter

DEC advised the public to avoid the tower after ice and wind damaged its top landing, pending repairs planned for later in 2017 (reported March 2017).
A volunteer from the Mount Adams crew replaced and repaired the tower's safety netting on May 13, 2017.
ADK High Peaks Foundation and nine volunteers mounted a new graffiti-resistant interpretive history sign on the tower's first landing on May 11.

The Student Conservation Association's Adirondack Corps painted and restored the tower, and volunteers fitted new cab windows between September and 4 October.
Friends of Mt. Arab refurnished the observer's cabin with period pieces so it looks as if the observer just stepped out (reported).

events.note: Volunteers worked on the tower on July 14, removing chicken wire and graffiti.

Graffiti was removed from the tower and cab, the footings repaired (with concrete work) and the flagpole rope replaced.

events.note: The tower dates from 1918; its centennial was celebrated in 2018.
A new observer's cabin was built at St. Regis in 1925.
Friends of St. Regis work crews carried out restoration in 2015; as of January 2016 the tower still needed some additional steel before it could be climbed.
Restored by the Friends, NYSDEC and the Student Conservation Association; a new roof was fabricated in June and the tower reopened on 1 September.
The 24 new cross braces flown in during October 2018 were all fitted; the footings were repaired, the steel under the treated steps primed and the tower painted.
Volunteers finished priming work on the St. Regis tower over two seasons, including cold-galvanizing drilled holes, and found corrosion in both areas (reported).
Volunteers carried interpretive panels up to the St. Regis tower on Sept 3, 2021 and installed them.
Through summer 2021 volunteers repainted the St. Regis tower and made minor repairs to its fencing; full fence replacement remained a priority.
Friends of St. Regis completed their painting project on the tower in spring 2022, hauling paint to the summit.
A board member of the Friends of St. Regis mounted a bracket on the tower so a US flag can be flown on steward days.
Two more panoramic view panels, west and north, were mounted in the cab, the third and fourth.
Friends repaired the old fence on Sept. 10 and installed one short section of new safety fence, with full replacement continuing into 2026.

events.note: The 60-foot Aermotor LS 40 tower was built in 1922 and first operated in 1923.
FFLA, Friends of Sterling Forest and volunteers began restoring the tower with work days from fall 2015, holding seven work dates in all.
The tower was reported closed to the public in early 2017, and the FFLA was working to reverse the closure (reported February 2017).
About 34 volunteers (Team Rubicon, Friends of Sterling Forest, FFLA, park staff) worked on the tower on 8-9 July; on 12 November volunteers replaced the last landings and steps.
New cab windows were made and fitted (fixed ones first, then the operating ones), paid for by ADK North Jersey/Ramapo; a volunteer stained the observer's cabin deck.
The engineer's inspection of the closed Sterling Forest tower was completed by August 2022, with the report still awaited.
Sterling Forest tower closed to the public pending an engineer's structural inspection, the same situation as Jackie Jones; still closed in late 2023.
